title: Poiseuille's Law and Stokes' Law

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Mechanical Properties of Fluids

expression: Poiseuille: V/t = πPr⁴/(8ηl)  ;  Stokes: F = 6πηrv  ;  Terminal velocity: vt = 2r²(ρ−σ)g / (9η)
explanation: Poiseuille's law gives the volume flow rate of a viscous liquid through a narrow tube — strongly (fourth-power) dependent on tube radius, so even a small change in radius produces a large change in flow rate. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag force on a small sphere moving through a viscous fluid, proportional to radius, viscosity, and velocity. Combining Stokes' law with gravity and buoyancy gives terminal velocity — the constant maximum speed reached when the net force on a falling sphere becomes zero (weight = buoyant force + viscous drag).

variables.meaning: Density of the sphere and of the fluid

workedExample.scenario: A small steel ball falls through a viscous oil and reaches terminal velocity.
workedExample.substitution: At terminal velocity, weight = buoyant force + viscous drag: (4/3)πr³ρg = (4/3)πr³σg + 6πηrvt

commonMistakes: Forgetting Poiseuille's flow rate depends on r⁴, not r² or r — a doubled radius increases flow rate 16-fold, not 4-fold, a frequent numerical-scaling error.
Omitting the buoyant force term when deriving terminal velocity — only weight minus BOTH buoyancy and viscous drag gives the correct zero-net-force condition.
genZNote: Poiseuille's law: double the tube radius, flow rate doesn't double — it goes up sixteen times.
